theme: Migration from paper, Excel, Brightwheel, or Procare

posts.post_content:
A childcare software migration should start smaller than most people think.

Export a sample.
Map the fields.
Look for duplicates.
Check one classroom.
Verify one billing scenario.
Then bring over the full set.

Moving fast on day one is less useful than moving cleanly.

A careful sample check keeps messy records from entering the new system and being mistaken for progress.
posts.review_status: writer self-reviewed: truth, source, humanization, brand, duplication, LinkedIn fit
posts.notes: Rewritten to remove goal/goal phrasing from migration opener.

posts.post_content:
Excel is not the enemy.

It is good at static lists: rosters, contacts, rate sheets, vendor lists.

The risk shows up when Excel is asked to prove time-sensitive work: ratio status at 10:15, subsidy attendance support, credential expirations, incident history.

That is the line directors should look for. Keep spreadsheets where they are useful. Move the high-risk operating record somewhere stronger.
posts.review_status: writer self-reviewed: truth, source, humanization, brand, duplication, LinkedIn fit
posts.notes: Uses the guide's distinction between Excel strengths and compliance-risk limitations.

posts.post_content:
Before cancelling old software, export the boring things.

Child records.
Family contacts.
Authorized pickup lists.
Billing history.
Payment records.
Staff certifications.
Attendance reports.
Subsidy documentation.

The boring things become urgent the first time a parent disputes a balance or a licensing question points to last year.
posts.review_status: writer self-reviewed: truth, source, humanization, brand, duplication, LinkedIn fit
posts.notes: Grounded in the pre-switch audit list from the switching checklist.

posts.post_content:
Do not make the software switch fight your billing calendar.

Mid-month cutovers split invoices. Mid-claim-period cutovers split subsidy records. Enrollment season adds changing family data on top of migration work.

A cleaner switch starts at a cleaner boundary: after the prior claim is handled, before the next billing cycle gets messy.
posts.review_status: writer self-reviewed: truth, source, humanization, brand, duplication, LinkedIn fit
posts.notes: Based on timing guidance around monthly billing and subsidy claim periods.

posts.post_content:
If you are leaving Brightwheel, the first job is not training.

It is export discipline.

Pull child roster data, family contacts, billing records, subsidy documents if applicable, and historical attendance. Review for stale enrollments, duplicate family entries, and outdated emergency contacts before import.

A migration is much easier when cleanup happens before the new system starts running the day.
posts.review_status: writer self-reviewed: truth, source, humanization, brand, duplication, LinkedIn fit
posts.notes: Uses the Brightwheel export and cleanup guidance without repeating unsupported claims.

posts.post_content:
A Procare migration deserves extra patience because records may live across modules.

Child and family data, billing history, staff records, subsidy authorizations, and CACFP records can each need their own export path.

The practical rule: do not assume one export means you have everything. Build a checklist by record type and confirm each file opens before cutover.
posts.review_status: writer self-reviewed: truth, source, humanization, brand, duplication, LinkedIn fit
posts.notes: Grounded in Procare data export complexity and record-type list.

posts.post_content:
Parallel running feels annoying because it is double work.

It is also the safety net.

For one billing cycle, the new system can become the primary record while the old system stays available as a reference. That is when missing rates, classroom mismatches, subsidy setup issues, and staff training gaps show up while there is still time to fix them.
posts.review_status: writer self-reviewed: truth, source, humanization, brand, duplication, LinkedIn fit
posts.notes: Uses the switching checklist's parallel running section.

posts.post_content:
Switching systems does not erase old record obligations.

Your historical Excel files, Brightwheel exports, or Procare reports may still be the proof for the period before cutover.

File them by year and record type. Attendance. Billing. Enrollment. Staff. Subsidy. CACFP, if applicable.

You do not need to keep editing the archive. You do need to be able to find it.
posts.review_status: writer self-reviewed: truth, source, humanization, brand, duplication, LinkedIn fit
posts.notes: Based on the guide's historical Excel archive guidance.

posts.post_content:
PebbleDesk supports CSV import plus Brightwheel and Procare migration presets.

That does not mean a director should import blindly.

The useful path is still sample export, mapping, preview, duplicate review, then full import. Migration support should make the work less brittle, not encourage teams to skip the checks that protect the record.
posts.review_status: writer self-reviewed: truth, source, humanization, brand, duplication, LinkedIn fit
posts.notes: States the supported import capability from the feature page and offering constants.

posts.post_content:
The hardest part of switching software is often not the software.

It is staff muscle memory.

A check-in screen moves. A billing step changes. A teacher who was fast in the old system feels slow for a week.

Plan for that. Train before cutover, give staff a short first-week reference, and name one internal person who can answer daily questions.
posts.review_status: writer self-reviewed: truth, source, humanization, brand, duplication, LinkedIn fit
posts.notes: Grounded in the checklist's staff retraining risk and go-live preparation.

posts.post_content:
A migration can look successful until billing day.

That is why rate structures need to be tested before go-live.

Pick a few real scenarios: full-time, part-time, sibling discount, subsidy family co-pay, one-time fee. Generate test invoices and compare them to the old expected amounts.

If billing is wrong, fix it before families see it.
posts.review_status: writer self-reviewed: truth, source, humanization, brand, duplication, LinkedIn fit
posts.notes: Uses go-live system configuration and billing continuity guidance.

posts.post_content:
For centers that accept subsidies, the migration question is specific:

Can the new system produce the attendance and claim support your state program expects for the next claim period?

Not someday. Not in a generic export. For the claim you will actually submit.

Run a test before cutover. Subsidy records are the wrong place to discover a format gap.
posts.review_status: writer self-reviewed: truth, source, humanization, brand, duplication, LinkedIn fit
posts.notes: Grounded in subsidy output verification and state-format warnings.

posts.post_content:
Do not turn a migration into a junk drawer transfer.

Inactive children marked active, duplicate guardians, old emergency contacts, expired staff credentials, outdated rates. If those move into the new system untouched, the new system inherits the old confusion.

Migration is a rare chance to clean the operating record before it becomes the next year's source of truth.
posts.review_status: writer self-reviewed: truth, source, humanization, brand, duplication, LinkedIn fit
posts.notes: Uses migration cleanup themes from Excel and switching guides.

posts.post_content:
A simple migration rule:

Do not cancel the old system until the critical exports are saved, the new records are validated, staff can run the daily workflow, and billing has been tested.

Cancellation is not the finish line. A clean first operating week is closer to the finish line.
posts.review_status: writer self-reviewed: truth, source, humanization, brand, duplication, LinkedIn fit
posts.notes: Based on backup plan and old-system access guidance.

posts.post_content:
A good childcare migration should feel careful, not heroic.

No mystery exports. No mid-cycle surprises. No lost attendance history. No staff learning the system while families are lined up at the door.

Just a clear path from the old record to the new one, with enough overlap that the director can sleep the night before cutover.
